section_summary: This section examines Japanese party organization and the January 1949 election, finding that personal loyalties, weak local branches, campaign restrictions, and funding shortages shaped political activity. It also contains a Soviet protest over police action at Tokyo labor demonstrations and General MacArthur’s reply. The final, continuing report surveys local elections through May 1, 1949, emphasizing independent candidates, uncontested races, and party strategy.

subfiles.title: Local Political Party Organization
subfiles.about: Transmits Jane M. Alden’s study of local Japanese party organization.
subfiles.summary: Huston describes weak conservative local branches, their dependence on Diet members and national headquarters, and the Communist Party’s stronger local organization.

subfiles.title: Local Organization and Activities of the Democratic Liberal, Democratic, and Socialist Parties
subfiles.about: Reports field observations on party branches in five prefectures.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum finds that conservative branches have small memberships, little money, limited local activity, and heavy dependence on national leaders and individual candidates. It compares Democratic Liberal and Democratic organizations in Kyoto, Shimane, Hyogo, Hiroshima, and Osaka, including the Democrats’ factional split and Tadokoro’s organizing work. It then examines Socialist efforts to rebuild labor support, tensions with union leaders, and Communist appeals to farmers and workers.

subfiles.title: Japanese Opinion of the Election Law
subfiles.about: Transmits Alden’s survey of election officials’ and party leaders’ views of election law.
subfiles.summary: Huston highlights complaints about inadequate campaign publicity, restrictions on parties, costly public management, and disagreement over electoral district size.

subfiles.title: Opinions of Japanese Election Officials and Leaders of the Major Political Parties Regarding the Election Laws
subfiles.about: Summarizes interviews about the operation and possible revision of Japanese election laws.
subfiles.summary: Election officials and party leaders criticize inadequate publicity, rigid rules for speeches and party activity, and the burden of election costs on local governments. They discuss campaign finance, ballot design, press and mailing rules, and the division of authority between election committees and local officials. Most favor a check-off ballot, while views differ on electoral district size.

subfiles.title: Soviet Protest over Japanese Police Action in Labor Demonstrations
subfiles.about: Transmits Derevyanko’s protest and MacArthur’s public response to Tokyo labor demonstrations.
subfiles.summary: Huston reports the Soviet letter, MacArthur’s blunt reply, and the possibility of further Soviet action in Allied bodies.

subfiles.title: Letter protesting police suppression of Tokyo labor demonstrations
subfiles.about: Accuses Japanese police of brutality during May 30–31 labor demonstrations.
subfiles.summary: Derevyanko alleges that police killed Kinji Hashimoto, injured and arrested other demonstrators, and violated democratic rights. He asks MacArthur to prevent further abuses and punish those responsible.

subfiles.title: General MacArthur’s Comment on General Derevyanko’s Letter
subfiles.from: Douglas MacArthur, General Headquarters Public Information Office
subfiles.about: Responds publicly to Derevyanko’s accusations about labor rights in Japan.
subfiles.summary: MacArthur calls the Soviet protest propaganda, defends Japanese labor protections, and condemns Soviet treatment of Japanese prisoners of war.

subfiles.title: Transmitting Copies of Report of Surveillance
subfiles.from: U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Encloses an Eighth Army report on local Japanese elections from January through May 1949.
subfiles.summary: Notes 628 elections, 2,947 candidates for 2,055 offices, and the limited influence of parties.

subfiles.title: Report of Surveillance: General and By-Elections, 1 January to 1 May 1949
subfiles.from: Legal and Government Division, Military Government Section, Eighth Army Headquarters
subfiles.about: Surveys local general and by-elections in Japan during the first four months of 1949.
subfiles.summary: The report explains election law and Army surveillance procedures, then tabulates 628 local elections and the predominance of independent winners. It analyzes uncontested rural races, turnout, and the uneven performance and tactics of the major parties, while warning that personal loyalties complicate comparisons of party strength. The excerpt ends during a discussion of local election strategy and a forthcoming Saitama gubernatorial election.
